description: Building an AI-enhanced mobile serious game! We use React Native and LLMs to create a dynamic "Space Mission Design Game" where players balance resources to survive. We are prototyping how AI adapts game scenarios for better engagement.
summary:
Orbit Architect is a playable space mission design game that teaches real mission engineering through play. Players pick a mission - Earth Observer, Lunar Mapper, Mars Weather Scout, Asteroid Sample Scout and more - then design a spacecraft, choose instruments, select a launch vehicle and orbit, and manage budget, mass, power, data and mission lifetime.

Every choice has a trade-off: a bigger camera adds science but also mass, power and cost. The Python simulation engine then calculates orbital period, Hohmann transfer delta-v, rocket equation, power and link budgets, and runs a month-by-month simulation with random events and a 200-run Monte Carlo forecast.

Players get a graded report out of 1000 explaining why the mission succeeded or failed, and can refly with a better design. It works solo or in a team of 2-4 with roles for Mission Director, Spacecraft Engineer, Science Lead, and Comms & Operations. It makes mission design — normally taught in separate pieces - understandable as one connected system.
details:
What it does:

Orbit Architect is a web game where you design and simulate a complete space mission in 6 steps: mission & crew, spacecraft, instruments, launch vehicle & orbit, simulation, and report. The live HUD shows budget, mass, power margin, data, science and lifetime as you build.

How it works:

The front end is HTML/CSS/JavaScript. All physics runs in Python (engine.py): orbital period T=2π√(a³/μ), circular and escape velocity, Hohmann transfer delta-v, inclination-change cost, Tsiolkovsky rocket equation with a 25% delta-v reserve, solar power by inverse-square law with eclipse fraction, battery depth-of-discharge, Friis free-space path loss and link budget, and mass budget with 20% contingency. The game (game.py) adds 3 difficulty levels, 12 random events scaled by your margins, scoring /1000, and Monte Carlo with 200 seeded runs showing success probability, mean score, P10 and P90.

Content:

8 missions, 8 spacecraft buses, 14 instruments, 8 launch vehicles (Falcon 9, Atlas V, Ariane 6, Vulcan, H-IIA, PSLV, Electron, SLS-style heavy) and 6 orbits, in data.py. Tests: 9/9 tests pass in test_engine.py. Sample results: Earth Observer 791.9/1000, grade B, Monte Carlo success 57%; Lunar Mapper 914/1000, grade S, success 90.5%.

Benefits and impact:

Students and beginners can learn why real missions fail - not enough power, a weak link to Earth, too much mass for the rocket - without needing a textbook. Team play teaches the different jobs in a real mission team.

Tools:

Python 3 (standard library only, no Flask), HTML, CSS, JavaScript, GitHub for code, Render for hosting.

Creativity:

Instead of a quiz or a video, the trade-offs are the game. A bad design still flies in the simulation - and then fails for a reason the report explains, so the player learns and tries again.
